paraphrase: Open bridge, unattributed: whatever can fail to be r (in the two-way sense of the potency of the contradictory, able to be r and able not to be r) can be otherwise in respect r. No source read for #352 states it. In Metaph. V, lect. 6 n. 14 (STMT-WHAT-CAN-BE-IN-MORE-WAYS-CAN-BE-OTHERWISE) supports it in part: it says that what can be in more ways can be otherwise, without the potency of the contradictory or the respect r. Met. V.5 does not state it (1015b11-13 argues the converse).
